audiences.label: Pastors
audiences.lead: Using your own preaching corpus for prep, audit, pastoral care, and series planning. Substitute the bracketed [items] with what you're actually working on.

sections.title: Sermon prep
sections.intro: Working out next week's sermon, or revising one in flight.

prompts.title: Have I preached on this passage?
prompts.prompt: Have I preached on [Ephesians 4:1-6] before? Pull every sermon that handles this passage, summarize what I said, and list any illustrations I used. Cite by sermon title and date.
prompts.what: Surfaces prior treatment of a passage so you don't unknowingly retread.

prompts.title: Pull my raw material on a theme
prompts.prompt: I'm preparing to preach on [grace under suffering]. Pull every sermon and sermon unit where I've touched on this theme. Group them by which angle I took.
prompts.what: Gets your own past thinking on the table before you start writing.

prompts.title: Synthesize what I've already said
prompts.prompt: I want to preach a single sermon that brings together everything I've said about [the cross]. Aggregate the strongest sentences and themes from my preaching on this — and tell me what's missing.
prompts.what: Builds a coherent synthesis from your own corpus, including the gaps.

sections.title: Avoiding repetition
sections.intro: Catching the illustration or angle you've leaned on too hard.

prompts.title: Don't let me retread
prompts.prompt: I'm preaching on [the prodigal son] this Sunday. Have I covered it before? What angle did I take, what illustrations did I use? I want to come in fresh — show me what to avoid.
prompts.what: Prevents accidentally giving the same sermon twice.

prompts.title: Illustrations I'm overusing
prompts.prompt: Pull a list of illustrations I've used more than once across my preaching. Group them by topic and tell me which ones are starting to feel like crutches.
prompts.what: Finds the patterns you stopped noticing in yourself.

prompts.title: What's recent
prompts.prompt: List my sermons from the last 12 months by date, with a one-sentence summary of each. I want a bird's-eye view of where I've been so I don't repeat myself.
prompts.what: A quick recap of your own recent direction.

sections.title: Series planning
sections.intro: Surveying past arcs before charting the next one.

prompts.title: Recap my last series
prompts.prompt: Walk me through my last sermon series, sermon by sermon. What was the arc? Where did I land? What did I leave underdeveloped that I might come back to?
prompts.what: Helps you see your own series' shape from the outside.

prompts.title: Pull raw material for the next series
prompts.prompt: I'm planning a series on [the book of Titus]. What sermons have I preached on Titus or its themes (leadership, doctrine, false teaching)? Pull them as raw material for the new series.
prompts.what: Mines what you've already done so the new series builds on it.

prompts.title: Three sermons that set the tone
prompts.prompt: Pick three sermons from my archive that represent how I want this next series to sound. Quote a representative sentence from each.
prompts.what: Gives you a voice/tone reference before you start writing.

sections.title: Pastoral care prep
sections.intro: Finding what you've said before a hard conversation.

prompts.title: Material for grief
prompts.prompt: I'm meeting with a member walking through grief. What have I preached on lament, suffering, or hope in death? Pull the most pastoral moments — direct quotes I could share or summarize in conversation.
prompts.what: Surfaces your own most tender material on a hard topic.

prompts.title: Material for doubt
prompts.prompt: Someone in my church is wrestling with doubt about scripture. What have I said in sermons that addresses this directly? Give me a list with brief summaries so I can prepare to talk with them.
prompts.what: Pulls a focused excerpt of your preaching on a specific issue.

prompts.title: Just the tender material
prompts.prompt: Pull anything I've preached on [the doctrine of assurance] that's particularly tender — meant for hurting people, not academic explanation.
prompts.what: Filters by pastoral register, not just topic.

sections.title: Self-knowledge / serendipity
sections.intro: Auditing your preaching, or letting the archive surprise you.

prompts.title: What I keep coming back to
prompts.prompt: What three scripture passages do I return to most across my preaching? Quote a representative sentence from each so I can see what I do with them.
prompts.what: Reveals the texts that anchor your preaching, sometimes invisibly.

prompts.title: Surprise me
prompts.prompt: Surprise me with three sermon units from at least a year ago. Pick ones that feel forgotten — maybe sermons I haven't thought about lately. Quote a striking sentence from each.
prompts.what: Resurfaces material you'd otherwise lose track of.

prompts.title: Honest audit
prompts.prompt: Across all my preaching, what's my dominant theme? Be honest. If you had to characterize what I'm always coming back to, what would it be — and what am I underweighting?
prompts.what: An outside-view summary of your own preaching's center of gravity.

audiences.label: Church members
audiences.lead: Using your pastor's preaching corpus for devotion, study, formation, and pastoral conversations. Substitute the bracketed [items] with what you're working through.

sections.title: After Sunday
sections.intro: Following up on the sermon you just heard.

prompts.title: Keep meditating on Sunday's sermon
prompts.prompt: I just heard my pastor preach on [the prodigal son]. Pull a related sermon or two from his archive so I can keep meditating on the theme this week. Cite by sermon title and date.
prompts.what: Extends Sunday into the week instead of letting it fade by Tuesday.

prompts.title: What did I miss?
prompts.prompt: I missed church last Sunday. What was the most recent sermon? Summarize the main points and the passages my pastor worked through.
prompts.what: A reliable recap when you couldn't be there.

prompts.title: Has he said this before?
prompts.prompt: My pastor said something striking on Sunday about [the kingdom of God]. Has he said similar things in other sermons? Show me where so I can dig deeper.
prompts.what: Connects a memorable line to a fuller body of teaching.

sections.title: Daily Bible reading companion
sections.intro: Pairing your devotions with your pastor's teaching.

prompts.title: Pastor on today's passage
prompts.prompt: I'm reading [Romans 8] in my devotions today. What has my pastor preached about this chapter? Give me a summary I can read alongside it.
prompts.what: Pastor's voice as a study companion to your Bible.

prompts.title: Work through a book
prompts.prompt: I'm working through the Book of [Ephesians] this month. Pull every sermon my pastor has done on Ephesians, in canonical order. I want to use them as a guide as I read.
prompts.what: Builds a one-pastor commentary on a book you're studying.

prompts.title: Hard text, help me sit with it
prompts.prompt: I'm wrestling with [Psalm 88 — it's a dark psalm]. What has my pastor said about lament or suffering that might help me sit with it instead of skipping past?
prompts.what: Brings pastoral help to a passage that's hard to read alone.

sections.title: Working through something
sections.intro: Bringing a life issue or doctrinal question to your pastor's teaching.

prompts.title: A hard season
prompts.prompt: I'm walking through [anxiety] right now. What has my pastor preached on this? Pull the most pastoral, gentle material — not just doctrinal explanation. I need encouragement, not a lecture.
prompts.what: Filters by pastoral tone, not just topic match.

prompts.title: Going deeper on a doctrine
prompts.prompt: I'm trying to understand [the doctrine of justification] more deeply. Walk me through how my pastor teaches it across his sermons. What does he emphasize? What does he warn against?
prompts.what: Builds a coherent doctrinal picture from many sermons.

prompts.title: Growing in a practice
prompts.prompt: I want to grow in [prayer]. What has my pastor said about it across his preaching? Pull the most concrete, actionable material — not just exhortations to do it.
prompts.what: Surfaces the how, not just the why.

sections.title: Family devotions & parenting
sections.intro: Adapting your pastor's preaching for the table or for talking with your kids.

prompts.title: A kid-accessible quote
prompts.prompt: I'm leading a family devotion this week on [the resurrection]. Find a kid-accessible quote or illustration from one of my pastor's sermons that I can share at the table.
prompts.what: Pulls something age-appropriate from adult preaching.

prompts.title: Teach my kids about a topic
prompts.prompt: I want to teach my kids about [forgiveness]. What has my pastor said about it in his sermons that I can adapt into something they can understand?
prompts.what: Raw material for parent-led teaching.

prompts.title: Talk with my teenager about doubt
prompts.prompt: Help me prepare to talk with my teenager about [doubt about the faith]. What does my pastor say about wrestling with hard questions? Pull the most honest, non-defensive material.
prompts.what: Gives you a posture and language for hard conversations at home.

sections.title: Find that thing I vaguely remember
sections.intro: When a sermon detail is half-remembered and you want to look it up.

prompts.title: Find the story
prompts.prompt: My pastor told a story in a sermon — something about [a man walking through a graveyard, I think]. I can't remember exactly. Help me find it.
prompts.what: Search by fuzzy detail when you can't remember the citation.

prompts.title: Find the quote
prompts.prompt: What was that line my pastor used about [contentment]? Pull a few candidates — I'll know it when I see it.
prompts.what: Like a memory aid for the line you almost remember.

prompts.title: Pull all the illustrations
prompts.prompt: Pull every illustration my pastor has used about [marriage]. I want to share one with a friend going through a hard season.
prompts.what: Treats the corpus as an illustration library.

sections.title: Hard questions
sections.intro: When you or a friend is asking something the faith has to answer.

prompts.title: Why does God allow suffering?
prompts.prompt: A friend is asking how a good God can allow suffering. What has my pastor said about this in his preaching? Pull the most thoughtful, non-defensive material.
prompts.what: Equips you to talk about hard things using your pastor's framing.

prompts.title: What does pastor teach about [X]?
prompts.prompt: How does my pastor handle [the doctrine of hell] in his preaching? Pull his clearest teaching on this. I want to understand it well enough to explain it.
prompts.what: A focused doctrinal pull on a specific question.

prompts.title: When the Bible feels off-putting
prompts.prompt: I'm struggling with how the Bible talks about [a hard topic, e.g. divine wrath]. What has my pastor said that might help me think through it instead of recoiling?
prompts.what: Brings pastoral framing to a text or theme that's hard to receive.
